To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we identified 46 BRCA1/BRCA2 variants, 38 of which were not associated with the disease and 8 of which were pathogenic.
we have screened the BRCA1/BRCA2/CHEK2/TP53 genes in a high risk population for HBOC and found a new mutation in BRCA2 gene, c.4829 + 4830delTG.
we found a new BRCA1 mutation in a Brazilian HBOC patient and the prevalence of the BRCA2 mutation c.4829-4830delTG in the Brazilian population is 6.8%.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of mutations in genes related to HBOCs in the Brazilian population, and the results can contribute to the development of genetic counseling and prevention programs.
the identification of pathogenic mutations in genes related to HBOCs, which is important for the development of more cost-effective genetic testing strategies in Brazil.
the identification of pathogenic mutations in the Brazilian population, and it is the first study of this kind in the Minas Gerais region.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the prevalence of BRCA1, BRCA2, TP53 and CHEK2 pathogenic mutations in Minas Gerais, Brazil, is similar to other countries, but the most prevalent mutations differ.

there are still many unknowns in the Brazilian population, especially in the Minas Gerais region, regarding the mutational profile of the genes involved with HBOC, and that the study of the mutational profile in the population is essential to establish the best strategies to be adopted in the clinical management of patients at high risk.
in this cohort of patients at high-risk for HBOC in Brazil, we found a high frequency of BRCA1 and BRCA2 pathogenic mutations, which is consistent with the literature.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

1) in this study, we identified 8 new pathogenic mutations in the BRCA1/BRCA2 genes and a probably pathogenic mutation in the CHEK2 gene in a cohort of patients at high risk of developing HBOC; and 2) the most prevalent mutation in the BRCA genes in this cohort was the c.4829-4830delTG in BRCA2 gene, which was not reported in the Brazilian population before.

the mutation spectrum of BRCA1 and BRCA2 genes in Brazilian patients with hereditary breast and/or ovarian cancer is similar to that described in other populations, with the exception of the c.4829 ~ 4830delTG mutation in BRCA2 gene that is more prevalent in the Brazilian population.

the prevalence of pathogenic mutations in HBOC patients in Brazil is higher than expected, and the prevalence of pathologic mutations is similar to the prevalence of pathogen mutations reported in other studies.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the p.R337H in TP53 gene can be associated to HBOC and not only Li-Fraumen syndrome, as previously described in the literature.

the prevalence of the BRCA2 c.4829 + 2T > G mutation is higher in the Minas Gerais region than in the rest of Brazil, and that the p.R337H variant in TP53 gene is not associated with Li-Fraumenic syndrome in our cohort.
